The proposed measurement is not invariant to prediction-preserving changes in logits. Adding the same feature-dependent scalar to every class logit leaves softmax probabilities unchanged but can substantially change the Jacobians, their hop distribution, and R. Section 6.1's coordinatewise softmax-monotonicity argument does not resolve this. The measurement therefore needs a more qualified interpretation or a formulation based on prediction-relevant quantities.

The experiments do not establish that R measures task requirements rather than topology and architectural propagation. For the paper's linearized GCN, H = S^L XW implies I(v,u) is proportional to (S^L)vu, so normalization removes dependence on the learned weights and task. Comparisons between road and citation networks cannot separate these factors. Controls using different target radii on the same graph, untrained models, and interventions on distant features would be substantially more convincing.

Several theoretical justifications are unsound as presented. Theorem 6.3 incorrectly assumes that a nontrivial smooth function necessarily has a measure-zero zero set; differentiability is insufficient. Lemma 6.7 incorrectly infers shell growth by differencing asymptotic ball-volume bounds, which does not establish the claimed pointwise bounds. Proposition 6.1 sums absolute derivatives of internal branches, whereas Equation (2) differentiates the final output, where the constructed branches have already canceled. These problems undermine the claimed theoretical foundation.

The synthetic target does not establish the claimed practical accessibility interpretation or unavoidable long-range dependence. Coordinates, road characteristics, and substantial label homophily provide potential shortcuts that the weak MLP comparison does not exclude. Coordinate-based predictors, label propagation, feature ablations, and stronger local baselines are needed.
